title: Disability and Purpose
definition: Disability and purpose means that physical, mental, emotional, developmental, or life limitations do not remove a person's value, dignity, calling, usefulness, or place in God's kingdom.
summary: Disability does not erase dignity, purpose, or usefulness before God.
christFocus: Jesus consistently showed compassion, dignity, and purpose toward people living with limitations, suffering, and physical challenges. Christ sees beyond human weakness and calls people according to His grace and purpose.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Scripture teaches that every person is created in the image of God and possesses inherent worth. Disability is part of living in a fallen world, but it does not diminish a person's value before God. Throughout Scripture, God repeatedly works through people who possessed limitations, weaknesses, fears, physical struggles, or personal hardships. The Lord often displays His strength through human weakness so that glory belongs to Him alone.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people living with disabilities are told by the world that their value is measured by productivity, independence, appearance, or physical ability. Scripture teaches the opposite. A person's worth comes from being created and loved by God. Understanding this truth protects believers from despair, comparison, shame, and feelings of uselessness.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not define yourself by limitations, diagnoses, injuries, or circumstances. Define yourself by your identity in Christ. Ask not only, "What can I no longer do?" but also, "How can God use me today?" Trust that God's purpose for your life remains intact even when circumstances change.
